takeaway: A neck tumour damaging the cervical sympathetic chain causes Horner's syndrome: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis, flushing and enophthalmos.

question.text: A 36-year-old man has a neck tumour damaging his left cervical sympathetic chain ganglion. Which physical sign would you expect?
question.say: A thirty-six-year-old man has a neck tumour. It has damaged his left cervical sympathetic chain ganglion. Which of the following physical signs would you expect?

answer.say: The answer is ptosis on the left.

lines.text: A man with a neck tumour on the left.
lines.say: This thirty-six-year-old man has a neck tumour on the left side.
The tumour has damaged the left cervical sympathetic chain, shown by the spark.
And look at his left eye. The lid droops. That is ptosis on the left.
The pupil is constricted. That is miosis.

lines.text: This is Horner's syndrome, with a dry face.
lines.say: This is Horner's syndrome. Loss of sympathetic supply also gives anhidrosis, facial flushing, and enophthalmos.

lines.text: Lateral deviation of the eye would mean the third cranial nerve.
lines.say: Lateral deviation of the eye would suggest damage to the third cranial nerve instead.

lines.text: Remember: sympathetic chain damage gives ptosis on the same side.
lines.say: Remember: sympathetic chain damage gives ptosis and a small pupil on the same side.
